tasks.short: Set editorial policy and direct publication teams, priorities, budgets and standards.

steps.what: Gather publication results, budgets, workload and unresolved editorial issues.
Compare reader feedback and editorial incidents with current policy.

loop.input: Reader feedback, editorial incidents and the current editorial policy.
loop.output: Cited issue clusters, policy gaps and alternative responses.
loop.check: Require source references; the editor checks coverage, disputed interpretations and missing viewpoints.
loop.stop: One pass per batch and one correction pass; unresolved cases return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules can count known categories but cannot reliably interpret new complaints or policy tensions.

steps.what: Discuss editorial direction, resources and competing priorities with department leads.
Write policy revisions and departmental objectives from agreed decisions.

loop.input: Recorded direction decisions, approved policy text and a policy template.
loop.output: Tracked policy revisions and measurable department objectives.
loop.check: Trace each substantive change to a decision; flag missing owners, limits and unresolved choices.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous decisions return to editorial leadership.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but agreed policy changes require contextual wording.

steps.what: Approve policy changes and resource commitments within delegated authority.
Publish approved policy, assign objectives and communicate changes to teams.

tasks.design: A dashboard joins publication, workload and budget data from the {CMS}, {PROJECT} and {ERP}; a bounded loop prepares cited policy options and tracked revisions in the {DOCS}. Leadership decides direction and approves commitments through the {WORKFLOW}, which releases the approved policy and assignments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results, incidents and policy versions sit in separate places. Editorial direction also depends on trust and contested priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and approval features handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes small connectors cheaper, while bounded text processing helps prepare policy revisions.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing commercial goals, editorial credibility and scarce staff remains leadership work. Inconsistent metrics can make a polished brief misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a commercially attractive policy damages reader trust, and secure support for difficult trade-offs.

ambition.what: Monthly review of underserved reader needs and publication capacity.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time assembling management papers and more time testing editorial direction with department leads. Formal budget and policy rights stay with existing delegates; no automatic expansion of authority is assumed.

reach.task: Choose which audience needs receive publication investment.
reach.learn: Audience segmentation, contribution margins and the limits of engagement metrics.

evidence.claim: Existing reporting, document versioning and approval workflows can support policy administration; this design is an implementation estimate.
Repeatable house-style checks can support policy implementation, but do not choose editorial policy.
A writing experiment supports drafting assistance, but does not establish savings for editorial leadership.

assumptions: This task describes a senior editor responsible for corporate publications in a mid-size company.
Publication results and budget reports can be exported without exposing individual employee performance.
Time shares describe a policy-management cycle, not the editor's entire week.
Access and consultation estimates include checking national rules and employee consultation where changes affect staff.
unknowns: The editor's actual policy, staffing and budget authority.
Which publication and finance data are available through supported exports or interfaces.
Whether proposed reporting introduces employee monitoring requiring consultation under national rules.
The quality and consistency of reader feedback and incident records.
research_questions: Does the brief preserve minority reader concerns as well as frequent complaints?
Can every proposed policy revision be traced to an approved decision?
Which existing reporting and approval features remove the need for custom code?
new_work: Check cited policy options for omissions and skewed interpretation.
Maintain shared metric definitions and source mappings.
Resolve missing ownership and conflicting policy versions.
Review access rights and consultation needs when reporting scope changes.

tasks.short: Coordinate publication projects with design, production and marketing colleagues, resolving problems together.

steps.what: Collect project status, latest proofs and unresolved production questions.
Arrange a meeting with the colleagues needed to resolve open questions.
Discuss proofs, negotiate trade-offs and agree how to resolve production problems.
Turn meeting notes into decisions, owners, deadlines and a written recap.

loop.input: Human-written decision notes and the meeting brief.
loop.output: Draft recap and structured actions with owners, deadlines and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link each action to its note; never infer agreement, owners or dates that were not recorded.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous actions return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes express commitments inconsistently; templates alone cannot extract them reliably.

steps.what: Send the recap, update project tasks and chase overdue actions.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} assembles a meeting brief from linked proofs in the {DOCS} and status in the {CMS}, while the {CALENDAR} handles scheduling. A bounded loop extracts actions from human notes; the editor approves them before the {WORKFLOW} updates tasks and sends reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proof versions and status are scattered, while action notes use inconsistent wording. Much of the meeting itself depends on people reaching agreement.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked records and calendar configuration cover preparation and scheduling. A small extraction loop can turn notes into reviewable actions.
tasks.still_hard: Creative disagreements, late changes and competing deadlines need direct conversation. Poorly captured decisions cannot be recovered reliably from incomplete notes.
tasks.human_edge: Read hesitation, resolve disagreements and negotiate a workable compromise without weakening the publication.

ambition.what: Earlier cross-functional resolution of proof and production conflicts.

tasks.altitude: The editor arrives with current proofs and leaves with a checked action list. Less chasing creates room for earlier problem-solving; decision rights remain shared with design, production and marketing leads.

reach.task: Assess whether proposed copy changes can fit the publication layout.
reach.learn: Layout constraints, visual hierarchy and the production cost of late revisions.

reach.task: Resolve conflicts between campaign deadlines and publication quality.
reach.learn: Campaign dependencies and the consequences of changing release dates.

evidence.claim: Calendar scheduling, linked project records and reminders are established configurable capabilities.
Extracting actions from human notes is a plausible bounded model use; the digest supplies no measured case for this meeting workflow.

assumptions: Most participants are internal colleagues; external supplier messages require separately agreed sending rules.
The design uses human notes and does not require meeting recording.
The meeting remains mainly human work, consistent with the relationship-heavy task.
Access estimates include checking national consultation requirements if the scope later adds recording or employee monitoring.
unknowns: Whether proofs and project tasks have stable identifiers and version links.
Which colleagues can commit to deadlines and production changes.
Whether existing meeting notes capture decisions and owners clearly.
Which scheduling and task features are already enabled.
research_questions: How often does action extraction invent agreement or miss an unresolved objection?
Can structured note fields remove the need for a model on routine meetings?
Does automatic preparation reduce time spent locating the correct proof?
new_work: Check extracted actions before assignments take effect.
Maintain project-to-proof links and participant lists.
Resolve contradictory deadlines and missing owners.
Adjust reminder rules when teams find them excessive.

tasks.short: Assess writers, interview candidates and negotiate approved employment or freelance terms.

steps.what: Define the writing need, budget and employment or freelance route.
Read applications or portfolios and choose whom to interview.
Interview writers about their work, judgement, availability and collaboration.
Select a writer using portfolio evidence, interview findings and the brief.
Negotiate scope, fees or salary, rights, royalties and payment milestones as applicable.
Prepare the appropriate offer or freelance contract from agreed proposed terms.
Approve the proposed commitment and resolve contract exceptions with relevant specialists.
Send the approved contract for signature and record the completed agreement.

tasks.design: Structured briefs and linked portfolios in the {ATS} and {DOCS} support human interviews and selection; no model ranks applicants. Approved fields populate employment or freelance templates in the {CLM}, the {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions and commitments for approval, and the {ESIGN} sends only the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Employment and freelance routes use different records and approvals. Negotiated rights and payment terms often arrive through conversations and correspondence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template, approval and signature features handle standard cases. Small connectors can transfer approved fields without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: Talent judgement, fair negotiation, copyright scope, royalty definitions and worker status remain contextual. GDPR, the EU AI Act where applicable, and national employment rules constrain changes to recruitment processing.
tasks.human_edge: Judge originality and editorial judgement, build a working relationship, and negotiate terms both sides understand.

ambition.what: First-time freelance contributors who need clear commissioning and payment terms.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time assembling contracts and following approval status. More time goes to portfolio discussions and contributor development; hiring, spending and signing rights remain with existing delegates.

reach.task: Turn a commission into a feasible scope, delivery plan and revision allowance.
reach.learn: Effort estimation, rights licensing and payment milestones.

reach.task: Plan the mix of staff and freelance writing capacity.
reach.learn: Capacity forecasting and the full cost of commissioning.

evidence.claim: Structured recruitment records, contract templates, approval routing and electronic signatures are established configurable capabilities.
The digest supplies no documented case showing that editorial hiring judgement or contract negotiation can be automated safely.

assumptions: Employment and freelance cases follow alternative routes; the steps describe a blended typical case, not two contracts per writer.
The editor acts as hiring manager where that responsibility is delegated.
Portfolio review and selection remain human; the records app only organises evidence.
Negotiation stays within delegated limits and does not itself issue a binding offer.
Access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: The proportion of employee hires versus freelance commissions.
Who may shortlist, select, negotiate, approve and sign.
Whether contract templates and clause alternatives have already been approved.
Which royalties, rights territories and payment structures are used.
Applicable national consultation duties and candidate-data retention periods.
research_questions: Can existing template configuration cover standard terms without custom drafting?
Does the route prevent unapproved terms or stale versions from reaching signature?
Which missing fields cause the most contract rework?
new_work: Maintain approved templates, rate guidance and routing limits.
Resolve nonstandard rights, royalties and worker-status questions.
Check failed record transfers and unsigned agreements.
Review access and retention for candidate and contributor records.

tasks.short: Create a reliable alphabetical or topical index with accurate page and chapter references.

steps.what: Obtain the current manuscript, pagination and indexing requirements.
Read the material and select meaningful concepts, names and index subentries.

loop.input: Versioned manuscript sections, indexing requirements and an existing term list where available.
loop.output: Candidate concepts, names and subentries with supporting passages and stable source anchors.
loop.check: Require supporting passages; reject absent terms and unsupported concepts; the editor reviews coverage and relevance.
loop.stop: One pass per section and one repair for invalid entries; unresolved sections return to manual indexing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Term matching handles known vocabulary, but a subject index also needs concepts expressed through varied wording.

steps.what: Standardise headings, merge synonyms and arrange entries alphabetically or topically.
Locate passages and add page ranges or chapter references to entries.
Check coverage, cross-references and page locations against the final proof.
Place the approved index into the publication and preserve its version.

tasks.design: A generator reads a versioned proof from the {DOCS}, uses a bounded loop to propose source-linked concepts, and applies deterministic term mappings, sorting and reference checks. The editor approves coverage and ambiguous headings before an integration inserts the index into the {DOCS} or {CMS}; pagination changes invalidate approval and trigger regeneration.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subject selection requires reading beyond exact keyword matches. Page references also become stale when layout changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can propose concepts with supporting passages. Deterministic anchors, sorting and pagination checks handle the mechanical work.
tasks.still_hard: Useful subject coverage is harder to validate than alphabetical order. Scanned files, complex layouts and weak source anchors can make reference mapping expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the terms readers will actually seek and distinguish substantial discussion from passing mentions.

ambition.what: A reusable cross-publication subject index for long-form marketing resources.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time locating pages and sorting entries, and more time improving reader navigation. With delegated approval, the editor can choose shared index headings; publication release rights do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Design a shared topic taxonomy for a resource collection.
reach.learn: Information architecture, controlled vocabularies and reader terminology.

reach.task: Keep index references accurate through layout revisions.
reach.learn: Document anchors, pagination dependencies and publication export formats.

evidence.claim: Sorting, approved synonym mappings, cross-reference validation and anchor-based location mapping are deterministic indexing techniques.
Source-linked concept extraction is a proposed bounded model use; the digest supplies no measured indexing case.
Documented failures in AI news answers support checking generated semantic content rather than accepting fluent output as evidence.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to long reports, guides and similar publications rather than every marketing article.
The proof contains extractable text and usable page or chapter identifiers.
Known synonyms use an approved term map; unfamiliar equivalences are flagged for human judgement.
Adding the index produces an internal proof, not automatic public publication.
Access estimates include approved processing of unpublished material and checking whether consultation applies.
unknowns: Which source formats preserve stable anchors through layout changes.
Whether the required index is a subject index, name index or controlled-term index.
Whether an approved taxonomy and synonym map already exist.
How often pagination changes after index approval.
Whether unpublished proofs contain personal or confidential information.
research_questions: How does concept coverage compare with an independently prepared human index?
Can page mappings survive insertion of the index and subsequent layout changes?
Which publications need semantic extraction, and which need only exact term matching?
Does the proposed cross-publication index improve readers' ability to find relevant passages?
new_work: Review proposed concepts and unfamiliar synonym relationships.
Maintain the shared term map and sorting conventions.
Resolve unmatched anchors and complex page ranges.
Sample omissions as well as incorrect entries.

role.altitude: The editor's week shifts toward editorial direction, contributor relationships, production decisions and reader navigation. Preparation, contract administration and index mechanics shrink; formal hiring, budget and publication authority changes only through explicit delegation.
reach: Marketing manager: connect editorial investment to audience needs and campaign capacity.
Graphic designer: resolve copy and layout trade-offs earlier.
Technical writer: develop shared terminology and navigation across publications.
Desktop publisher: preserve reference accuracy through layout changes.
skills_to_grow: Source-based review of generated text and extracted actions.
Audience research and interpretation of publication metrics.
Contract scope, rights and payment literacy.
Workflow configuration, access controls and exception handling.
role.ambitious_version: An editor who connects audience needs, contributor capacity and production constraints, using reliable preparation to make better publication decisions and offer a searchable collection of long-form resources.
